title: Isandro and the Hollow Anew
premise: Isandro Dunmore has spent her life as a royal food-taster in the valley of Hollowmere, where magic cannot follow and the old kingdom of Vessia survives only in memory. When the usurper King Aldric declares a hunt for anyone carrying the gift, Isandro discovers her slow-built immunity to poison is itself a magic the valley was designed to suppress — and she is dragged from the only home she's known into a country that officially no longer exists. Guided by a disgraced cartographer, a hedge-witch healer, and a boy who can hear doors, she searches for the Door of Anew, the last threshold out of hollowed Vessia, before Aldric's armies reach the free cities. In the end, Isandro learns the door opens not to escape but to choice: she seals it behind her, choosing the fragile found family she made over any kingdom, and plants the first seed of a new Vessia in the free cities' borderlands.
about_author: Astrid Oyelaran is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of countries that no longer exist, an obsession that bleeds into everything she writes. She lives at the edge of a valley and writes about the people who leave it.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. We meet her in the palace kitchens of Hollowmere, sipping a laced broth meant for the regent and feeling nothing — as always. Establishes her routine, her pride in her strange immunity, and her quiet loneliness among servants who keep her at arm's length. Emotional beat: contentment with a hairline crack of longing.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Well
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Criers announce King Aldric's Edict of Cleansing: all bearers of the gift must be surrendered or hunted. The kitchen goes silent; the head cook burns something in the hearth. Isandro realizes the edict describes symptoms she half-recognizes in herself. Beat: dread arriving in daylight.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She tests herself privately — a candle flame bends toward her finger. Magic cannot follow into Hollowmere, yet something in her answers anyway. Terror and wonder war as she buries the evidence. Beat: the self she knew is gone by morning.

chapters.title: The Regent's Kindness
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The regent, Dame Ovelin, summons her for a private tasting and watches too closely. Kindness here is a trap; Isandro understands she is being measured. She lies for the first time in her life and hates how easily it comes. Beat: betrayal anticipated, loyalty curdling.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Gate
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Aldric's hunters arrive wearing grey hoods, carrying a device that hums near hidden gifts. They take the stable-boy Tam first. Isandro watches from a window, doing nothing, and the shame brands her. Beat: guilt as a door opening.

chapters.title: Running Water
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She flees through the mill-race at night, where the humming device loses her trail. First time past the valley's edge in her life; the world outside is terrifyingly wide. Beat: exhilaration braided with grief for everything left behind.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Nothing
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Introduce Sef Ardenne, a disgraced royal cartographer exiled for mapping Vessia — a country that no longer exists on any sanctioned chart. He recognizes what Isandro is before she says it. Beat: wary alliance struck over a fire.

chapters.title: A Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef explains the truth: Vessia wasn't conquered, it was unmade — its name struck from records, its magic hollowed into valleys like Hollowmere. The Door of Anew is the last way through the erasure. Beat: the scale of the lie revealed.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Hears Doors
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. They find Perrin, a feral twelve-year-old hiding in a waystation, who can hear every locked thing 'humming.' He hears something enormous under the mountains: the Door. He attaches himself to Isandro without asking. Beat: reluctant family forming.

chapters.title: Grey Hoods on the Road
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Hunters ambush them at a river crossing. Isandro's immunity lets her drink a poisoned wine offered as 'parley' without flinching, buying their escape and horrifying the hunters. Beat: her curse becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch of Marrowfen
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Introduce Wren Ostara, a hedge-witch healer who amputates hope for a living, patching refugees Aldric's purge has broken. She agrees to guide them to the free cities — for a price she won't name yet. Beat: grief given a profession.

chapters.title: What Wren Buried
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback woven through present: Wren once healed hunters' victims by hiding their gift, and lost her sister to the pyre for it. Her unnamed price is revealed: someone must carry her sister's ashes through the Door. Beat: sorrow shared is weight halved.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Glow
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. The party glimpses the free cities' lights — sanctuary, trade, noise, life. Perrin, who has never seen a city, is overwhelmed; Isandro realizes she wants this for him more than escape. Beat: hope with a horizon.

chapters.title: Sanctuary Has a Price List
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Inside the free city of Callowmark, they learn refugees with the gift are tolerated only as registered labor. Sef must choose between selling his maps of Vessia — his life's work — to fund their passage. Beat: dignity traded for survival.

chapters.title: The Registry
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Registering means a brand and a leash; refusing means the hunters find you. Isandro registers under a false name and feels the brand-iron's heat as a promise she makes to herself instead. Beat: defiance disguised as compliance.

chapters.title: Aldric's Voice
chapters.summary: Interlude, hunter-captain Veyra's POV. Veyra, leading the hunt, interrogates a captured Tam and learns a taster fled Hollowmere. She begins assembling a profile of Isandro — and admires her. Beat: the enemy gains a face and a mind.

chapters.title: Maps of the Unmade
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Studying his confiscated-and-rebought maps, Sef finds the pattern: the Door of Anew moves, following the old coronation road, and will surface at the Stone Choir within one moon. Beat: a deadline set by geography.

chapters.title: The Thief in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Working in a Callowmark inn, Isandro tastes a dish meant for a magistrate and detects poison no one else can — saving him and exposing herself to attention. Beat: her nature refuses to stay hidden.

chapters.title: Veyra Comes to Dinner
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Captain Veyra arrives at the inn, courteous, lethal, asking questions over supper. A duel of manners across a table; Isandro serves her soup she has tested three times. Beat: terror performed as grace.

chapters.title: Tam, Alive
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam escaped the hunters and reaches Callowmark half-dead, carrying word that Aldric's armies march on the free cities early. Reunion with Isandro cracks her open — the boy she failed to save saved himself. Beat: guilt answered by forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Vote at the Hearth
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The five argue: run to the coast, or race to the Stone Choir for the Door. Wren forces the real question — is a door an exit or a beginning? They choose the Door. Beat: found family becomes a deliberate choice.

chapters.title: Leaving Callowmark
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. They slip out ahead of Veyra's net; Perrin hears the city's ten thousand locks sigh as they go. He asks Isandro if she'll leave him too; she promises badly and means it completely. Beat: attachment confessed sideways.

chapters.title: The Coronation Road
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. On the ancient road, Sef reads the landscape like text — standing stones, erased milestones, names scratched out by decree. Walking the unmade country, Vessia flickers at the edges of vision. Beat: history haunting the present.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembered
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A village off every map still keeps Vessian customs in secret — bread baked with a coin inside, songs in the dead tongue. An elder gives Isandro her grandmother's ring, recognizing Dunmore blood. Beat: belonging deeper than citizenship.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ford
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Veyra corners them at a ford; a fight leaves Sef wounded and one hunter dead by Isandro's hand — her first killing. Veyra withdraws, unsettled, ordering no pursuit until she understands what Isandro is. Beat: innocence spent, irrevocably.

chapters.title: Fever and Ashes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sef's wound festers; Wren works through the night while Isandro holds him down. Wren confesses her fear that the Door is a story she needs to be true. Beat: faith tested at a sickbed.

chapters.title: What Immunity Costs
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro realizes her immunity isn't absence of magic but a sealed vessel — the valley didn't suppress her gift, it corked it, and the cork is failing. Every day she grows stranger, stronger, less herself. Beat: power as erosion.

chapters.title: The Stone Choir
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. They reach the Stone Choir, pillars that sing when wind passes. Perrin hears the Door beneath them, patient as a heartbeat. But so does something else — Veyra's devices, converging. Beat: arrival and trap in one breath.

chapters.title: Aldric's Herald
chapters.summary: Interlude, Aldric's POV (brief). The usurper, dying of a poison no taster caught years ago, needs gifted blood to hold his unmaking spell together. Veyra reports the Door found. His orders: take them alive. Beat: villainy given a wound and a motive.

chapters.title: The Singing Opens
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At moonrise the Choir sings the Door of Anew partway open — enough to show a threshold of light and a country that might exist again. Hunters strike. Battle among the stones; Wren burns her healing gift as a weapon for the first time. Beat: sanctuary defended with violence.

chapters.title: Veyra's Choice
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. With Isandro at blade's length, Veyra hesitates — she has hunted a person, not a prize, and knows what Aldric's ritual requires. She lowers her sword and turns on her own grey hoods. Beat: the enemy becomes an ally at cost.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Door demands a toll: one bearer must remain on the threshold, holding it open, or it seals forever. Wren steps forward with her sister's ashes — it was always her price. The party refuses to let her go alone. Beat: sacrifice met with solidarity.

chapters.title: Through the Threshold
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro crosses first and finds not paradise but potential: unmade Vessia, raw and waiting to be named again. She understands the Door doesn't lead out — it leads back, to before the erasure. Beat: revelation reframing the whole journey.

chapters.title: Aldric at the Choir
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Aldric arrives with his army, dragging Tam as bait. He offers Isandro a bargain: her sealed vessel of magic in exchange for the others' lives. Beat: the climax's terrible arithmetic laid out.

chapters.title: The Unsealing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro agrees — then, at the moment of transfer, uncorks everything at once. The immunity breaks; decades of stored magic floods the Choir. The stones sing the true name of Vessia, and Aldric's unmaking spell unravels around him. Beat: the curse weaponized, the self risked entirely.

chapters.title: What the Door Decides
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. The Door, fully awake, offers each of them passage anywhere — even back to ordinary lives. One by one they refuse it, choosing each other over escape. Wren scatters her sister's ashes into the light. Beat: theme made flesh — belonging chosen, not granted.

chapters.title: Sealing the Anew
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro seals the Door behind them, keeping only a seed of its light in her grandmother's ring. Aldric, unmade by his own erasure, fades with the country he tried to kill twice. Beat: catharsis; the hunt ends by ending its reason.

chapters.title: Borderlands, Planted
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Spring in the free cities' borderlands. The five — plus Veyra, pardoned by usefulness rather than law — break ground on a settlement with no king, no registry, no brand. Isandro plants the seed of light. Beat: quiet joy after ruin.

chapters.title: The Taster's Table
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Final chapter: Isandro cooks for her family, tasting every dish first out of habit, feeling warmth where poison used to pass. Perrin sets the table; Sef draws a new map with one blank space labeled 'ours.' Beat: belonging, at last, served warm.
